clue.text: With training, you or I belong in science

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so these letters are put through their paces into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A careers pitch: with the right training, you or I could have a place in science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With training' reads like a career promise; 'training' is the anagram signal for YOU OR I BELONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurobiology is a branch of biological study, the scientific study of the nervous system, so it is an example of a science.

clue.text: Knitwear against counter absorbs big drops of water

indicators.note: running counter to the reading direction means the letters are taken backwards
the phrase absorbs the answer, holding it within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A woolly jumper that soaks up heavy drops of rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbs' marks a word held inside 'Knitwear against' (ARAGAIN, across the word break), and 'counter' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is a famous waterfall, and a waterfall is a place where water takes a big drop, so the plural suits the falls.

clue.text: King of Britain left off King of Georgia's middle name

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter for left is removed from the name

parts.note: Martin Luther King Jr, born in Atlanta, Georgia, had Luther as his middle name

explanation.surface: A puzzle about royal names, one British king and one Georgian king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King of Georgia' suggests a monarch; it is Martin Luther King, from Georgia in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the legendary ruler of Britain in Arthurian tales, the father of King Arthur.

clue.text: Supported by state before maturity, is toeing the party line

indicators.note: before places the state ahead of maturity in the answer

parts.note: a thing supported by another rests on it
a state, as in 'what a state', is a mess
maturity is coming of age

explanation.surface: A politician backed by the state before growing up, who sticks to the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who repeats the official policy is said to stay on message, the idiom for toeing the party line.

clue.text: One running a Scottish island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a small Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Prepare to exercise leg, perhaps, and clean back

parts.note: a leg is an example of a limb

indicators.note: back means the word for clean is read from its end

parts.note: clean means pure

explanation.surface: A gym warm-up: stretch a leg and wash your back.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to loosen the muscles with stretches, getting ready for exercise; the idiom matches the phrase.

clue.text: Information about artistic style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Seeking information about an artistic style.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of art, music or writing, so it is a style of artistic work.

clue.text: In the morning, cook, in case I forget

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the morning hours, ante meridiem

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A note to oneself: cook in the morning, in case I forget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a kitchen job; it is the anagram signal for IN CASE. The definition is what such a person would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with amnesia suffers memory loss, so 'I forget' is a fair description of what such a person might say.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by greed, I tormented journalist

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed within these words, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A confession: consumed with greed, I tormented a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor works in journalism, overseeing and correcting what reporters write, so the answer is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: A director in nursing home, male, is attacking a person's character

indicators.note: nursing means holding, as if cradling, so the home wraps round the in

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director working in a care home attacks someone's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing home' reads as one place; 'nursing' is the signal that HOME holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem argument goes after the person instead of their case, the Latin phrase meaning 'to the person'.

clue.text: Become crazy nationalist instead of good migrant

indicators.note: instead of says one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: to become crazy is to go mad

explanation.surface: A nationalist driven mad by a good migrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home who moves from place to place, much as a migrant does.

clue.text: Extremely deficient game is over

indicators.note: deficient at the extremes, so the game loses its outermost letters

parts.note: lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks

explanation.surface: A team performing very badly, and the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and across are synonyms as prepositions, as in a bridge over the river or a bridge across it.

clue.text: Let off steam about European border in earnest

indicators.note: about means going round, so the vent surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to vent is to let off steam
a hem is a border on cloth

explanation.surface: Someone ranting about a European frontier, in all seriousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and passionate, so an earnest, intense manner fits the adjective.

clue.text: Lost when river filters into another

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: filters into means seeps inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: another river, the Tay, the longest in Scotland

explanation.surface: A rower getting lost where one river flows into another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second river, the Tay in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off its course, so it is lost.

clue.text: With too much capitalisation, have typo corrected

indicators.note: a typo that is corrected has its letters put right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor's note: too many capital letters, so the typo has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalisation' looks like capital letters; in finance it is the capital a company is funded with.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that is top-heavy has too much capital or too many senior staff relative to its base, the business sense of capitalisation.

clue.text: India probes pliant rupee dealer

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so India enters the word for pliant

parts.note: pliant means supple
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the abbreviation for the rupee, India's currency

explanation.surface: India investigates a trader who is soft on the rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier provides goods for sale, so a trader or merchant who deals in them is a dealer.

clue.text: Matter-of-fact shareholder's meeting welcomed by idiot in charge

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so the meeting goes inside the word for idiot

parts.note: prat is British slang for an idiot
AGM is the annual general meeting of a company's shareholders

explanation.surface: A businesslike shareholders' meeting chaired by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic person deals with things practically and realistically, which is a matter-of-fact approach.

clue.text: Footwear affected in training regime

parts.note: a boot is an item of footwear
camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated

explanation.surface: Fussy footwear worn in a fitness regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is an intensive programme of physical training, originally for military recruits, so it is a training regime.

clue.text: Encounter naked figure not at all quietly somersaulting

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the word for figure loses its outer letters

parts.note: a figure is a shape

indicators.note: somersaulting means flipping over, so this stretch is read backwards

parts.note: not at all means none, as in 'none the wiser'
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Stumbling on a naked figure doing very quiet somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips S and E off SHAPE; 'somersaulting' turns NONE plus P into PENON.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen on something is to come across it by chance, an idiom for meeting or encountering it.

clue.text: A milder form of hell will, we hear, disrupt routine

indicators.note: we hear says the pieces are only heard, so the entry matches their sound, not their spelling

parts.words: A milder form of hell will
parts.note: heck is a mild substitute for the swear word hell; 'll is the short form of will

explanation.surface: A mild swear word will, we're told, break the daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'routine' means a comic's act, not a daily habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler shouts at a comedian or speaker during their act, interrupting the performer's set.

clue.text: The best way to release something that's stuck, say a spigot?

indicators.note: say signals the phrase is spoken, so the entry matches its sound

parts.words: The best way to release something that's stuck
parts.note: a jammed thing is freed when you force it

explanation.surface: Advice for a jammed tap: what's the best way to free it?
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, 'force it' and FAUCET sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a tap or valve controlling the flow from a barrel or pipe, the same thing Americans call a faucet.

clue.text: Breast lift husband is wanting for Communist sympathiser

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast

indicators.note: is wanting means is lacking, so the letter for husband is removed

parts.note: to hoist is to lift

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery news: a breast lift that a husband wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' reads as desiring; here it means lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A Titoist follows Josip Broz Tito, the communist leader of Yugoslavia, so is a communist sympathiser.

clue.text: Antiseptic creams or soap? Test half of each

indicators.note: half of each says take the front half of every one of these words in turn

explanation.surface: A lab instruction: compare antiseptic creams or soap by testing half of each.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote, the wood-tar distillate, has long been used as a disinfectant and preservative, so it is an antiseptic.

clue.text: Charming way to secure Number One

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast round something, so the street holds the other piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
number one is a child's word for a wee

explanation.surface: A charming way to get to the top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number One' suggests the top spot; it is nursery slang for urinating, a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes someone pleasant and endearing, a synonym for charming.

clue.text: Reveal I am Sting making a comeback

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a sting operation is a trap set to catch criminals

explanation.surface: A rock star announcing 'I am Sting, back on tour'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' looks like the singer; it is a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on or make it known, so it means to reveal.

clue.text: In hospital department, torso cut into quarters

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the torso goes within the department

parts.note: A and E is the accident and emergency department of a British hospital

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a torso is the body

explanation.surface: In casualty, a torso is cut into four pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests cutting into four; it means lodgings. A&E is the British casualty ward.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a home or dwelling place, and quarters means lodgings where someone lives.

clue.text: Make noise like a dog to court female

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Barking like a dog to win a woman over.
explanation.definitionFit: Woof is the sound of a dog's bark, and as a verb it means to bark.

clue.text: Raised bank loan, at first, the day before venture's termination

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: termination is the end, so the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A bank that raised a loan the day before a venture ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; it is an embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment built up along a river to stop flooding, a raised bank of earth.

clue.text: American in favour of insurrection initially claiming disgraceful riot could be with stronger reason

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so these letters surround the rearranged riot

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of insurrection
disgraceful signals the word riot being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An American backs an uprising whose shameful riot is reasoned more strongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraceful' makes TIOR from RIOT, held by FOR and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin logic phrase: an argument holds all the more firmly in this case.

clue.text: Café puts back five units regularly having narcotic effect

indicators.note: puts back means read from the end, so the café words run in reverse
regularly takes every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: A café serving five units of something with a narcotic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts back' reverses CAFE PUTS into STUPEFAC, then the alternate letters of 'five units' give IENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupefacient is a drug that dulls the senses, so having a narcotic effect describes it.
